subject: Agriculture
title: Agroecology vs. Industrial Scale
description: One-minute skill: Agroecology vs. Industrial Scale.

hook.text: Can small, ecological farms feed the world? Or do we need industrial scale? The debate splits experts.

buildup.text: Small farms produce 30% of global food on 24% of cropland. They're more productive per hectare than large farms.

discovery.text: Agroecological methods can match industrial yields while preserving biodiversity and soil health.

twist.text: Industrial agriculture feeds cities efficiently through supply chains that small farms can't easily access.

climax.text: The answer isn't one or the other—it's appropriate scale for each context, with support for both.

punchline.text: Small farms are efficient. Large farms are connected. Both are needed.

quiz.question: What share of global food do small farms produce?

details.summary: The debate between agroecology and industrial-scale farming centers on whether small, diversified farms or large, high-input operations are better suited to feed the world sustainably. This topic compares both approaches on yield, ecology, and social impact.
details.whyItMatters: How we choose to farm determines both our food security and environmental future. The right balance between agroecological and industrial approaches will shape whether agriculture heals or harms the planet.
takeaways: Industrial agriculture produces high yields but at significant environmental cost
Agroecological farms show greater biodiversity and resilience to climate shocks
Small farms produce 30% of the world's food on less than 25% of farmland

faq.question: What is the difference between agroecology and industrial agriculture?
faq.answer: Industrial agriculture uses high inputs—fertilizers, pesticides, machinery—to maximize yield on large monocultures. Agroecology applies ecological principles like biodiversity, crop rotation, and biological pest control to farm sustainably with minimal external inputs.

faq.question: Can agroecology produce enough food to feed the world?
faq.answer: Research suggests agroecological methods can match industrial yields for many crops while being more resilient. Combined with reducing food waste and dietary shifts, agroecology could contribute significantly to global food security.
